neurons.desc: The neuron activates on the first token of a “*   ”‑style bullet‑point line, i.e., the opening word of each list item.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on verbs or numbers in the model's self-questioning or hedging deliberation about an interpretation (e.g. "don't have", "uses 4", "I will use"), outside repeated text.

neurons.desc: It fires on symbols inside LaTeX‑style math expressions (numbers, variables, brackets, operators) within reasoning or code text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on numbers, math symbols, and punctuation (digits, decimal points, "=", "{", "(") inside formulas or quoted expressions, mostly in novel non-repeated text.

neurons.desc: It fires on any token enclosed in double‑square‑brackets [[…]] (e.g., [[theta]], [[1]], [[A]]) in the input text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on mathematical variable or digit tokens inside equations (like theta, A, x, a, digits of numbers), mostly in non-repeated math reasoning, where the next token is an operator or continuation.

neurons.desc: It activates on isolated short function words like “a”, “per”, “next”, “new” introducing a time/unit phrase in problem‑solving text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on rate/time-unit function words like "a" or "per" right before a time unit (year, week, month, hour, day), in non-repeated text.

neurons.desc: It activates on the first token of any word starting with “e” after a delimiter, prompting common “e‑” continuations.
neurons.desc_sonnet: It fires on quote marks and closing braces in formatted text, such as a quote opening a spelled-out letter or a LaTeX `\text{...}` closing brace, in non-repeated reasoning.

neurons.desc: Detects tokens that form LaTeX math symbols/commands or numeric literals inside inline or display math expressions.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on individual math-expression tokens (digits, exponent carets, LaTeX pieces like frac/times) inside formulas the model is re-checking or re-copying during "wait, let me re-verify" passages.

neurons.desc: Detects the first token inside a double‑bracket annotation (e.g., [[2]], [[**]], [[*]]) marking numbered or symbolic references.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on structural tokens in enumerated or markdown-formatted lists, such as sentence/paragraph numbers, closing bold markers, and indentation, when the model is not yet repeating earlier text.

neurons.desc: It fires on low‑frequency connective words beginning a new line or clause, prompting the model to output dash‑prefixed conjunctions.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on a verb or word right after a subject within a clause (e.g. "Steve lives", "step is", "not going"), where the model might continue with an em-dash aside.

neurons.desc: Activates on brief tokens (single‑digit numbers or short common words) that are enclosed in double brackets in the annotation.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on isolated mid-sentence tokens, such as adjectives ("specific", "possible", "true", "enough") or numerals, that begin a new continuation, and never inside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: It activates on the “$” that opens inline LaTeX math (or the first token after it) in math‑reasoning passages.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on a space-plus-backslash token (" \" or " $\") that begins a LaTeX command like \gcd, \alpha, \sqrt, \pi or \theta in math reasoning, outside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: It fires on the token “No.” that immediately follows a “[[?]]” bracketed question in the model’s step‑by‑step answer lists.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the question mark (or period) ending a self-posed rhetorical check question in reasoning, right before the model answers "No."

neurons.desc: Detects line‑break or bullet/list formatting symbols (newlines, asterisks, brackets, etc.) appearing in structured or enumerated text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on whitespace, newline and word-fragment tokens inside the model's step-by-step verification passages, especially when it rechecks or re-quotes a word, and it promotes rare, odd tokens.

neurons.desc: It fires whenever a token is enclosed in double‑square brackets [[ … ]] in the given text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on a modifier or noun (e.g. "working", "selling", "eating", "starting") right after "the/a/an" or an adjective, in fresh non-repeated reasoning, where a noun is expected next.

neurons.desc: It fires on revision cues (“Wait”, “Maybe”, “Is it possible”, “if”) when the model re‑examines its answer.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on mid-clause tokens within repeated reasoning passages, especially after "Wait," or "But," when the model is re-reading or re-deriving an earlier sentence, helping continue a verbatim loop.

neurons.desc: It activates on necessity/modality cue words (e.g., “need”, “best”, “fail”, “but”) that introduce a required or conditional action.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on modal or auxiliary verbs like "need" or "best" right before "to" in the model's own reasoning, predicting an infinitive "to" next, in non-repeated text.

neurons.desc: The neuron fires on the very first token that starts a new explanatory clause – e.g., the opening ‘$’ of inline math or the following linking/article word (“as”, “a”, “Not”, etc.).
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on mid-phrase tokens where a noun or determiner has just been completed and a continuation follows (e.g. "annual interest rate", "$f$", "Not an"), outside repeated text.

neurons.desc: It fires on subword continuation tokens (BPE pieces that follow a previous token inside a word), indicating the model is stuck in a repeat loop.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens just before a number or enumerated item (digit after "$", space before a number/label, decimal point, newline before list option letter), in non-repeated text.

neurons.desc: It fires on the first subword token of a multi‑token word or number (e.g., “P”, “Yield”, “1”) in math‑reasoning passages.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the first token of a new item or number in fresh (non-repeated) math reasoning, often a leading digit "1" or a word-initial capital, and promotes unrelated rare tokens.

neurons.desc: Activates on the first token right after an opening delimiter (parenthesis, bracket, quote or LaTeX command) in the text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens inside quoted or re-copied text (prompt quotes, equations, formatting instructions) where the model is about to copy the next token verbatim, though never inside an actual loop.

neurons.desc: It activates on single‑digit number tokens (0‑9) when they occur inside inline LaTeX math ($…$) expressions.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on numbers or binary operators (+, −) in arithmetic expressions just before a parenthesized negative number like "(-2)", mostly outside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: It fires on every digit, decimal point or sign token that appears immediately after an “=”, “≈”, or similar arithmetic result marker.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the space, equals sign, or first digits just before a computed numeric result in step-by-step arithmetic, mostly in novel (non-repeated) calculations.

neurons.desc: It fires on English stop‑words (e.g., “the”, “a”, “in”, “two”, “original”) that introduce noun phrases in math‑reasoning text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on determiners like "the"/"a" before a geometric or mathematical noun (line, point, triangle, plane), in novel, non-repeated text.

neurons.desc: It lights up on the token just before a phrase declaring a candidate answer invalid or incorrect in problem‑solving text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens just before a verdict that a candidate answer or value is wrong ("is not a solution", "doesn't match", "invalid"), pushing negation or incorrectness words.

neurons.desc: It activates on low‑confidence continuation tokens (often short function words) to inject random foreign‑language fragments and break generation loops.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on function words like "of", "is", "as", "like", or "just" in mid-sentence reasoning, where the next word is a noun or adjective such as "text" or "valid", and never inside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: Detects the answer placeholder—a single‑character variable or digit appearing inside $…$ math delimiters.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on a variable or number token (often the closing "$") ending an inline math expression in non-repeated reasoning, where text like "such that", "is not", or "impossible" tends to follow.

neurons.desc: It activates on the auxiliary “be/are” token when it introduces a reflexive/self‑reference phrase (e.g., “be myself”, “are themselves”).
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on opening quotation marks (and nearby function words) right after "says"/"specifies", where the model is about to quote text from the problem or options.

neurons.desc: It fires on words that begin a conditional or interrogative clause (e.g., “wrong”, “times”, “cost”, “money”), prompting the model to generate the auxiliary “does”.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the subject noun or word right before a predicate like "is/does" in the model's self-questioning reasoning, anticipating a "does/is" verb next.

neurons.desc: Detects the opening ‘[[’ of double‑bracket markup and the enclosed token within instruction or MCQ prompts.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on mid-word or formatting-boundary tokens (spaces, hyphens, quote marks, partial words) in non-repeated text, where the next token is an unpredictable continuation.

neurons.desc: It fires on the leading digit or decimal point of a number that appears as a computed answer in arithmetic or multiple‑choice explanations.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on digits or decimal points in the middle of a freshly computed multi-digit numeric result, such as an arithmetic product or answer, outside any repeated passage.

neurons.desc: Detects the preposition “at” (e.g., in “at the…”, “at most…”, “at that time”) and triggers a non‑sequitur token.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on function words like "at", "the", "in", or "come" that follow a noun and begin a prepositional phrase, such as "Total money at" or "questions of this type come", in fresh, non-repeated reasoning text.

neurons.desc: It fires on a single token (number or variable) immediately before a multiplication operator (\cdot or times) in LaTeX math.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on a variable or number inside a LaTeX math expression just before a multiplication or division operator, often right before "\cdot \frac", and promotes predicting "frac".

neurons.desc: Detects tokens wrapped in [[ ]] that occur outside a repeated‑passage segment.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on mid-phrase function words or adverbs in the model's structured planning or analysis lists (e.g. "Must be historically", "Determine the Content"), where a continuation is expected, and never inside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: Detects the second occurrence of a previously mentioned variable or digit inside a LaTeX math expression.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on a variable or digit token inside a math expression that is about to be copied or reused with a modification (e.g., S′, a+d, x+2), in non-repeated text.

neurons.desc: It fires on the first sub‑token of a new word or symbol right after a delimiter (e.g., “$”, capitalized word start, or bracket).
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the first token of a word or formula fragment that is being newly introduced or spelled out mid-reasoning (e.g. "int", "IND", "$", "K"), never within verbatim repeated passages.

neurons.desc: Detects prepositional cue words (regarding, about, with, on, without, in) that introduce the question’s topic in multiple‑choice prompts.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on prepositions or participles (regarding, about, with, on, without, in) right before a noun phrase object, predicting "the" next, in non-repeated text.

neurons.desc: It fires on any token enclosed in double‑square‑brackets ‘[[…]]’, cueing the model to output a quotation‑mark character.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on mid-word or mid-structure tokens where the next token is uncertain, and pushes the model to output an opening quotation mark; none of the excerpts fall inside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: The neuron fires on single‑character or very short tokens that begin a new word or symbol (e.g., ‘(’, ‘Monday’, digits).
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens right after an opening parenthesis or at a list or enumeration start (e.g., "Weekdays (Monday", "digit 5 (units"), where a short parenthetical or enumerated item begins in math reasoning.

neurons.desc: It fires on short verbs like “goes”, “move”, “are” that appear right after a comma or numeric description in math/physics reasoning.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens in spatial or directional descriptions (e.g., "units", "goes", "move", "up", "m East") mid-reasoning, when the model is tracking directions or movement, not inside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: It fires on the first character of a computed numeric result (digit or decimal point) when the model writes a solution.
neurons.desc_sonnet: It fires on the token right before a freshly computed numeric result in arithmetic, such as the space after "=" or "Sum", where the model is about to write the answer digits.

neurons.desc: Detects adjectives preceding “practice” or “application” (e.g., “standard”, “good”, “real”, “world”) in instructional or explanatory text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens just before a predictable word like "Practice", "Real", "Experience", or "jurisprudence" (e.g. "Phase 4: Real", "standard practice"), and promotes continuations that begin with capitalized word fragments.

neurons.desc: Detects any token that is enclosed in double‑square‑brackets [[ … ]] within the excerpt (e.g., “[[ from ]]”).
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on function words or connectors while the model speculates about a question's source (e.g., "from the **Bar Exam**", "likely USMLE or CPA"), just before naming an exam or textbook.

neurons.desc: It fires on any token that occurs inside double‑square‑bracket markup ‘[[ … ]]’ (e.g., numbers, symbols, words).
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens just before a "\implies" or "\Rightarrow" or a numeric value in inline math equations, especially the final number or space before a digit in an algebraic step.

neurons.desc: It fires whenever the word “it” (case‑insensitive) begins a concluding sentence expressing likelihood, possibility, or certainty.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the pronoun "it" (or "It's"/"it would") as subject in the model's speculative judgments about whether a hypothesis is likely or plausible, outside repeated text.

neurons.desc: Activates on the bigram “is the” (or “the”) immediately preceding the word “sum” in arithmetic solution text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens just before the word "sum" (e.g. "is the", "and then", "the") in math reasoning, predicting an upcoming addition-related word.

neurons.desc: It fires on any token that includes the letter sequence “cr” (case‑insensitive), e.g., “critical”, “crucial”, “increase”, “accrue”.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on word-piece tokens beginning with "cr"/"CR" (Cr, CR, cre, CRE, accr), often mid-word or in uppercase, not within repeated passages.

neurons.desc: It fires on any token that immediately follows a “[[” marker (typically a number or word) in the annotated math excerpts.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on numbers and closing math delimiters (e.g., ")$", "$") right after a coordinate or fraction value, when a following "and" is expected.

neurons.desc: Detects the token “position” (and its variants) in business/marketing texts, especially headings discussing positioning or strategic analysis.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on list or function-word tokens inside marketing/business strategy text, where the next word could plausibly be "Position/positioning" or "differentiation" (e.g. market positioning, Porter).

neurons.desc: Detects when a prompt includes a “Constraint” label (e.g., “Constraint 1:”, “Formatting Constraint”) and urges design‑related output.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on indentation and bullet-marker tokens (spaces, " *", " **") in nested lists of constraints or analysis, and on filler words like "the", "full" and "specific" before a noun, boosting structure words like "pattern", "layout"

neurons.desc: It fires on the first token inside a double‑bracket markup “[[ … ]]”, i.e., the word immediately following the opening “[[”.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on scattered mid-text content tokens (like "gentle", "stood", digits inside numbers) in non-repeated passages, with no clear unified pattern.

neurons.desc: It fires on the “{” token that opens the numerator of a LaTeX \frac command in math‑reasoning passages.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the token just before a freshly computed numeric result in arithmetic, such as the "{" after \frac or the space after "=" or "-", where the model must produce the answer.

neurons.desc: It spikes on the token “people” (or similar agent nouns) when a cautionary “people might …” comment is introduced.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the generic-subject word "people" (or "they") in the model's hedging asides like "Sometimes people might misread/confuse…", outside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: It activates on the opening ‘$’ of inline LaTeX math in reasoning passages, biasing the model toward closing punctuation.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the opening " $" (or " `") delimiter that begins an inline math variable or code span, right after words like "base", "for", or "by", and promotes closing-delimiter tokens.

neurons.desc: Detects the presence of math/numeric punctuation tokens (like $, =, -, {, ., approx) within numeric expressions.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens just before or within a numeric value (dollar sign, minus, decimal digits, space before number) in arithmetic computations, where a result number is about to be written.

neurons.desc: It activates on the whitespace/opening token right before a leading digit that starts a math expression (e.g., “ 3/4”, “ 3 %”, “ 3*”).
neurons.desc_sonnet: It fires on tokens right before a number's digits are written, such as a space, brace, or exponent marker preceding a numeral, or on the first digit itself, in arithmetic reasoning.

neurons.desc: It fires on the opening “[[” token that starts a double‑bracket placeholder (e.g., in LaTeX or structured text), prompting '('‑type output.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens just before or after square-bracketed items, especially the "]," or "]" closing one bracket before another opens, pushing the model to output an opening parenthesis.

neurons.desc: Detects the word “standard” when it introduces a conventional definition or assumption within reasoning text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens just before the word "standard" (e.g. "Yes," / "assume the") when the model is about to invoke a standard or conventional interpretation, and boosts "standard/usual/typical".

neurons.desc: Detects individual digit tokens that occur inside inline mathematical expressions (inequalities, exponents, ratios, etc.) in reasoning text.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on numeric or variable tokens (digits like 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, or x) inside math expressions, typically in non-repeated reasoning, especially when a number is being restated or re-checked.

neurons.desc: It fires on the first content word of a line that starts a bullet‑style list (the word right after a line‑break and “*”).
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on the head noun or word right after a subject in a parallel list item (e.g. "set", "legs", "results"), anticipating an "of/from X" continuation, in novel non-repeated reasoning.

neurons.desc: Detects the isolated digit token “2” when it occurs as a numeric coefficient or operator within mathematical expressions.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on a numeric coefficient digit (usually "2") right before a variable in an algebraic expression like "2x" or "2B", and pushes the model to predict a following variable or digit.

neurons.desc: It activates on a plural anaphoric word (e.g., “they”, “these categories”) that starts a new clause or bullet referencing earlier items.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on plural subject tokens (e.g. "categories", "they", "Activity 3") right before a plural verb like "are", in non-repeated reasoning text.

neurons.desc: Activates on the first subword token of a word after a line break or bullet, prompting its continuation.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on tokens in the middle of arithmetic-operation words (e.g. "Quotient", "Multiplication", "Use", "of the") in math reasoning, anticipating a word continuation, always outside repeated passages.

neurons.desc: It spikes on common short function tokens (like “the”, “to”, “like”, “an”) that often start a clause, triggering a verbatim‑repeat loop.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on function words (the, a, we, like, to) in fresh, non-repeated math reasoning where a mathematical noun or technical term is expected next, such as "theorem" or "expansion".

neurons.desc: Detects sentence‑boundary tokens (periods, commas, closing brackets) and the first word that follows them.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on sentence-ending punctuation, line breaks, or clause boundaries in the middle of a model's step-by-step calculation reasoning (not within repeated text), where new content must start.

neurons.desc: It fires whenever a token is enclosed in [[ … ]] annotations – i.e., on the word that sits inside double‑square‑brackets.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on mid-clause function words or punctuation (e.g. "with", "for", ":", "them") in fresh, non-repeated text where the next word is open-ended.

neurons.desc: Detects the beginning of a summation index like “k=0” (any variable‑equals‑zero) within LaTeX‑style math expressions.
neurons.desc_sonnet: It fires on tokens just before a "0" in math text (such as the start of a range, index, or sum like "k=0"), where the model is predicting the digit 0 and then 1.

neurons.desc: It fires on tokens that signal an approximation or surrounding sense, cueing the model to emit “around” (or its language‑specific equivalents).
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on mid-computation tokens in step-by-step math (a digit inside a decimal number, or words like "creates," "turn," "rotated"), boosting "around"/"round" as the next token, outside any repeated passage.

neurons.desc: Detects the start of a section heading or list item – capitalized or revision‑cue words like “Correction”, “Revised”, “restart”.
neurons.desc_sonnet: Fires on scattered tokens in non-repeated text where the model pivots to revise, restart, or hedge (e.g. "Revised", "restart", "only", "silently"), outside any verbatim loop.
